text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu slams Palestinian police "terrorism". Palestinians find bomb factory in Bethlehem.
- Foreign Minister David Levy willing to meet Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat at European Union.
- 25 hurt in Israeli Supreme Court protest by Druze.
- Hospital workers to strike today.
- Israeli coalition chairman Meir Sheetrit of Likud party: No to gas monopoly accepted by Treasury and National Infrastructure Ministry.
- Madge Networks of Israel plans 10 to 20 percent job cuts. The Tel Aviv company makes communications products.
- Israel Electric Corporation to raise $1.3 billion on U.S., German markets.
- Pharmos Corp and Chiron Corp announce pact to jointly market technology designed to make protein-based drugs such as insulin and beta interferon more effective.
GLOBES
- Treasury chiefs and defence chiefs meet on Monday to specially discuss the defence budget for next year.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu: Change in election law would steal mandate from the public.
- Levy refuses to promise concessions as a condition for meeting Arafat in Brussels.
- Justice Minister Tsahi Hanegbi set up a non-profit fund against traffic accidents and received a salary during the election run-up.
- Government approves law to prevent compensating intifada wounded. Bill could get first Knesset reading next week.
- Treasury: Cut 3.5 billion shekels. Army and health ministry: Add billions.
- Gottex swimwear company owners consider companies that could buy control.
MAARIV
- Israel demands Arafat suspend police commander.
- Former Finance Minister Dan Meridor will announce he is running against Netanyahu for prime minister.
- Tickets to September 30 U-2 concert at Ramat Gan Stadium go on sale on Tuesday. Prices from 199-269 shekels ($50-$75).
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Hamas "death factory" uncovered near Bethlehem.
- Signs of a majority for initiative to change the direct election law.
- Huge deal at Koor industrial concern: Foreign investor buys about $30 million in shares.
